extension.description: Explore code rework trends by AI attribution across repositories, directories, and files in your IDE.
workspace.trust: Indexing requires reading Git objects in the workspace.
commands.showLineDetail: code-evolution-lens: View Current Line Rework Trends
settings.ref: Local Git ref to analyze. The default `HEAD` is the checked-out commit; examples: `main` or an existing `origin/main`. The extension never runs fetch automatically. Refresh the index after changing this setting.
settings.detectAiMessageMarkers: Also recognize markers in commit bodies, subject tags, and prefixes. Default: `false`. Set to `true` to recognize `[claude]`, `aider:`, and `Generated with Cursor`. Attribution trailers such as `Co-authored-by` are always recognized according to the configured rules, regardless of this switch.
settings.aiProviders.description:
Enter an array of AI tool rules, one object per tool. Defaults cover 68 Agent families, including TRAE, Codex, OpenClaw, Qoder, and Pi.
provider: Required display name, such as "TRAE". This field itself is not matched.
nameTokens: Whole words or phrases in names in the final attribution trailer block, case-insensitive. ["claude"] matches Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 noreply@anthropic.com, but not McClaude. Email addresses in angle brackets and Generated-By, Assisted-by, and Created-by are also supported. The trailer block must be at the end of the message, separated from the body by a blank line. Ordinary author/committer names are not matched. No detectAiMessageMarkers switch is required.
emails: Complete email local parts before @. ["internal-codebot"] matches internal-codebot@company.example in the author, committer, or final attribution block. Matching ignores case and domains. Do not enter full addresses, wildcards, or numeric account IDs. For GitHub's numeric-ID+copilot-swe-agent[bot]@users.noreply.github.com, use ["copilot-swe-agent[bot]"] and retain [bot]. Plus signs in ordinary email addresses are preserved. Generic names such as noreply and agent may produce false positives. No message-marker switch is required.
bracketTags: Tags inside square brackets in the commit subject, without brackets. ["trae"] matches a subject starting with [trae] Fix cache. Only the subject is checked, case-insensitively. Tags use 2–31 ASCII letters, digits, spaces, or _ . -, starting with a letter or digit. Requires detectAiMessageMarkers: true.
messageMarkers: Fixed text in the commit message. ["Generated with Cursor"] matches this text anywhere in the subject or body, case-insensitively, using literal substring matching without regular expressions. Requires detectAiMessageMarkers: true.
subjectPrefixes: Fixed prefixes with punctuation at the start of a subject. ["aider:"] matches aider: Fix authorization checks; a prefix immediately followed by a letter, digit, or underscore does not match. Matching is case-insensitive. Requires detectAiMessageMarkers: true.
All fields other than provider are string arrays. Supply at least one matching rule. Any match in an enabled field or array is sufficient; omit a field or use [] to disable it. Minimal example: [{"provider":"TRAE","nameTokens":["trae"]}]. Custom arrays replace the defaults; append tools to the existing array to preserve them. Rules for the same provider name are merged. detectAiMessageMarkers defaults to false. Default product names and tags do not imply tools automatically write Git attribution. Without Git markers, AI use cannot be identified. See the bundled PROVIDERS.md for sources.
settings.aiProviders.markdownDescription:
Enter an array of AI tool rules, one object per tool. Defaults cover **68 Agent families**, including TRAE, Codex, OpenClaw, Qoder, and Pi.

- **`provider`**: Required display name, such as `"TRAE"`. This field itself is not matched.
- **`nameTokens`**: Whole words or phrases in names in the final attribution trailer block. `["claude"]` matches `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 noreply@anthropic.com`, but not `McClaude`. Matching ignores case and supports `Name <email>`, `Generated-By`, `Assisted-by`, and `Created-by`. The block must be at the end of the message, separated from the body by a blank line. Ordinary author/committer names are not matched. **No message-marker switch is required**.
- **`emails`**: Complete email local parts before `@`. `["internal-codebot"]` matches `internal-codebot@company.example` in the author, committer, or final attribution block. Matching ignores case and domains. Do not enter full addresses, wildcards, or numeric account IDs. For GitHub's `numeric-ID+copilot-swe-agent[bot]@users.noreply.github.com`, use `["copilot-swe-agent[bot]"]` and retain `[bot]`. Plus signs in ordinary addresses are preserved. Generic names such as `noreply` and `agent` may produce false positives. **No message-marker switch is required**.
- **`bracketTags`**: Tags inside square brackets in the subject, without brackets. `["trae"]` matches `[trae] Fix cache`. Only the subject is checked, case-insensitively. Use 2–31 ASCII letters, digits, spaces, or `_ . -`, starting with a letter or digit. **Requires `detectAiMessageMarkers: true`**.
- **`messageMarkers`**: Fixed text in the commit message. `["Generated with Cursor"]` matches this text in the subject or body, case-insensitively, using literal substring matching without regular expressions. **Requires `detectAiMessageMarkers: true`**.
- **`subjectPrefixes`**: Fixed prefixes with punctuation at the start of a subject. `["aider:"]` matches `aider: Fix authorization checks`; a prefix immediately followed by a letter, digit, or underscore does not match. Matching ignores case. **Requires `detectAiMessageMarkers: true`**.

All fields other than `provider` are string arrays. Supply at least one matching rule. Any match in an enabled field or array is sufficient; omit a field or use `[]` to disable it. Minimal example: `[{"provider":"TRAE","nameTokens":["trae"]}]`. Custom arrays replace the defaults; append tools to the existing array to preserve them. Rules for the same provider name are merged. `detectAiMessageMarkers` defaults to `false`. Default product names and tags do not imply tools automatically write Git attribution. Without Git markers, AI use cannot be identified. See the bundled `PROVIDERS.md` for sources.
settings.aiProviders.provider.title: Tool Display Name
settings.aiProviders.provider.descriptio: Required string shown in attribution details, for example `"Claude Code"` or `"Internal Coding Assistant"`. The name itself is not matched. Supply at least one `nameTokens`, `emails`, or message-matching rule.
settings.aiProviders.nameTokens.title: Name Keywords in Attribution Trailers
settings.aiProviders.nameTokens.descript: Array of tool keywords or phrases in names in the final attribution block. `["claude"]` matches `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 noreply@anthropic.com`. Also supports `Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>`, `Generated-By`, `Assisted-by`, and `Created-by`. The block must end the message and be separated from the body by a blank line. Ordinary author/committer names are not matched. Use just `claude` to cover model and version suffixes; do not enter a whole trailer, email address, or regular expression. Matching is case-insensitive and respects whole-word/phrase boundaries; `McClaude` does not match. No `detectAiMessageMarkers` switch is required. Omit or use `[]` to disable name matching.
settings.aiProviders.emails.title: AI Email Local Parts
settings.aiProviders.emails.description: Array of names before `@` in email addresses. `["internal-codebot"]` matches `internal-codebot@company.example`. Do not enter full addresses, `@`, domains, or wildcards; full addresses are rejected. Matches authors, committers, and final attribution trailers, ignoring case and domains. `["copilot-swe-agent"]` also matches GitHub's `numeric-ID+copilot-swe-agent@users.noreply.github.com`. Plus signs in ordinary addresses are preserved. Generic names such as `noreply` broaden the match. No `detectAiMessageMarkers` switch is required. Omit or use `[]` to disable email matching.
settings.aiProviders.bracketTags.title: Bracket Tags in Commit Subjects
settings.aiProviders.bracketTags.descrip: Array of tags inside square brackets in commit subjects, without the brackets. `["claude"]` matches `[claude] Add permission cache`; do not use `["[claude]"]`. Use 2–31 ASCII letters, digits, spaces, or `_ . -`, starting with a letter or digit. Only the subject is checked, case-insensitively. Requires `detectAiMessageMarkers: true`. Omit or use `[]` to disable subject tags.
settings.aiProviders.messageMarkers.desc: Array of fixed text written by the tool into commit messages. `["Generated with Claude Code"]` matches this text in the subject or body, case-insensitively, as a literal substring. Regular expressions and wildcards are not supported. Avoid broad terms such as `AI`. Requires `detectAiMessageMarkers: true`. Omit or use `[]` to disable message-text matching.
settings.aiProviders.subjectPrefixes.des: Array of fixed prefixes at the start of commit subjects, including punctuation. `["aider:"]` matches `aider: Fix authorization checks`; `fix: aider: Fix authorization checks` does not match. Prefer a colon followed by a space. A prefix immediately followed by a letter, digit, or underscore does not match. Matching ignores case; regular expressions are not supported. Requires `detectAiMessageMarkers: true`. Omit or use `[]` to disable subject prefixes.
settings.excludeGlobs: Exclude paths from new-code metrics, matched relative to the repository root. For example, `**/thrift_gen/**` excludes generated directories at any depth. Custom arrays replace the default list; retain defaults you still need. Previously counted lines remain tracked if moved into excluded paths.
settings.decorations.enabled: Show subtle, normal-weight `ai` (AI-assisted additions) and `rw` (first-modification regions still locatable today; shown as `改` in Chinese) before verified editor lines. Hover for attribution and rework details. Scrolling reuses verification; split editors are independent. Editing, branch changes, or stale snapshots clear markers. Default: `true`. Set to `false` to hide markers without changing trend statistics.
